C1.worst_defect: The hero says what it is ("Point of sale for Vendure", "Pre-release · plugin 0.3.0") but never says who should not use it or how it compares with what a Vendure merchant would otherwise pick (Shopify POS, Square, Lightspeed). Four equal-weight CTAs (Live demo / Quick start / Try with your store / GitHub) compete, and "Try with your store" stalls until the plugin is installed.

C2.worst_defect: Refunds and the customer note work in the live demo, and the At the till description promises "refund a till sale and close the day", but both need "the plugin release after 0.3.0", which has no date or milestone. The changelog's last release is 0.3.0 on 2026-10-06, six weeks before capture, which a sceptic reads as stalled. The footer says "MIT licensed", yet building the till needs "your own RxDB Premium licence token in RXDB_PREMIUM" (Limitations). No maintainer or company is named anywhere I could see.
C2.where: home.desktop.02 comparison table; at-the-till.phone.01 description; changelog.desktop.01; limitations.desktop.01; home footer

C3.worst_defect: The quick start is thorough but long (9 steps plus lettered sub-steps a–i; 9 phone slices). A gotcha lives only on Connect a till: the till's order list needs ReadOrder, which the vendurepos-pos-till role "gains only in the release after 0.3.0", so it must be added by hand. The quick start's step 9 check ("order.create v4 and register v1") does not surface that.

C4.worst_defect: The changelog is written for the maintainer, not the evaluator: "ADR 0005", "order.create v5" and bare "#116"/"#117" with no link or plain-English effect. Breadcrumbs in search are only "VendurePOS". The docs pages themselves (troubleshooting, notifications, connect a till) are clear and concrete.

C5.worst_defect: The hero product screenshot is cropped mid-row, and the feature cards are eight identical boxes with no visual hierarchy. The docs sidebar's grey panel appears to stop partway down long pages (around y≈900). Otherwise the design is clean and restrained, and dark mode is solid.

C6.worst_defect: The phone hero screenshot shows "Cart (4) · €59.59" beside "Guest · 3 items" (an inconsistency a sceptic notices) and a truncated "Q..." column header. The quick start runs to 9 phone slices with no on-page TOC beyond the section dropdown. There is no horizontal overflow, and the type is readable.

C7.worst_defect: Every sitemap lastmod is the build time (2026-11-17/18), not the content date, so it tells crawlers nothing. The SoftwareApplication JSON-LD has no softwareVersion even though the hero states 0.3.0. llms.txt repeats the At the till "refund a till sale" claim for an unreleased feature. Lighthouse is 98/100/100/100 with CLS 0, the 404 is correct, and there are no overflow or alt failures.

overall_worst.defect: Refunds at the till are shown working in the live demo and promised in the At the till description ("refund a till sale and close the day") and llms.txt. They actually need "the plugin release after 0.3.0", which is undated and unlinked, while the newest release is 0.3.0 from 2026-10-06, six weeks earlier. A competitor-aware sceptic advising a client would call that demo-ware on a stalled project.
overall_worst.where: at-the-till.phone.01 / at-the-till.desktop.02, home.desktop.02 comparison table ("Not yet: it needs the plugin release after 0.3.0"), changelog.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Ship the release, or give it a target date and link its milestone or issue wherever "release after 0.3.0" appears. Drop "refund a till sale" from the At the till description and llms.txt until it ships. Add a dated "latest activity" line or a roadmap link to the changelog so six quiet weeks don't read as abandonment.
